title: Finite and generic reductions for residue-chain independence
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, $n\geq1$, and $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$. On Noetherian excellent schemes with $\ell$ invertible [def-exc-excellent-ring], use ordinary etale $D^+$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] and the geometric costalks, twists, and normalized immediate residue maps of [def-per-potential-dualizing-complex]. For a finite chain $\gamma$ of codimension-zero or immediate geometric specializations let $T_\gamma^a(M)$ be their composite on costalk cohomology in initial degree $a$, with all intervening twists. For $c\geq0$ let $P_c$ assert equality of these composites for any two chains with the same geometric composite of codimension at most $c$, for every such scheme, every $M\in D^+$ and every initial degree. Let $Q_c$ be the restricted assertion for normal integral excellent strictly henselian local schemes of dimension at most $c$, chains from geometric generic to closed point, $M=\Lambda$ and initial degree zero [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring, def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. Then $P_c$ holds if and only if $Q_c$ holds.
More precisely, chain equality is preserved and reflected by the finite-residue exceptional comparisons for a finite morphism and a lifted geometric specialization [lem-per-finite-residue-gysin-naturality]. After strict localization it can be tested on the reduced closure of the general point with the exceptional restriction of $M$. On an integral strictly local scheme of dimension $r$, testing in initial degree zero reduces first to $\tau_{\leq0}M$, then to $\mathcal H^0M$; for sheaves the test depends only on restriction to a dense open. Finally the test reduces, by a finite normal cover trivializing a constructible generic sheaf and by finite exceptional restriction, to the constant sheaf on a normal strictly local scheme. Arbitrary initial degree is obtained by replacing $M$ by a cohomological shift.
